issues.description: Re-ingest clears warnings/stats but not results, so removed input rows remain in the database as stale data.
Ingest commits rows incrementally, so a later parser crash can leave a partially updated database.
Harness B parser assumes each JSONL value and metrics field is a dict; valid non-object JSON crashes ingestion.
Malformed XML is not caught and untrusted XML parsing is not hardened, so one bad file aborts ingest.
Non-finite scores such as NaN are accepted by parsing and can crash on database insert instead of warning/skipping.
Required identity fields are not validated; blank run_id values can silently overwrite each other via the unique key.
Harness A CSV headers are ignored, so reordered or wrong columns are parsed positionally into bad data.
Invalid JSONL is recorded as missing_score, masking a distinct data-quality failure mode.
Timestamp parsing rejects common RFC3339 forms with offsets or fractional seconds, causing unnecessary skipped rows.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the requested target directory without guardrails.
Tests only cover generated fixture behavior and miss changed-input reingest, malformed JSON/XML, blank IDs, and non-finite scores.
